title: A 50 km Roman aqueduct crossed a river on three tiers of arches
body: The Pont du Gard in southern France stands about 48 metres high. Its stacked arches carried the water channel across the Gardon as part of a roughly 50 km route supplying Roman Nimes.
takeaway: Keeping the channel above the valley let water continue along its carefully graded path by gravity.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Pont du Gard
visual: three tiers of stone arches spanning a wide river valley
